routing_warnings.description: The instruction to select three standout moments with no required topic primarily specifies source and moment selection rather than changing the initial batch assignment.
The requirement for selected moments to have effective hooks belongs to the independent hook-quality Requirement.
The instruction to produce a clean edit belongs to the independent visual-editing Requirement.
The finding that one clip was too short and the new 30–90-second rule concern the independent clip-duration Requirement.
The instruction to add color to captions concerns the independent caption-presentation Requirement.
The pause on making additional clips applies to future recurring production, not the already completed extended trial batch.
The new assignment for three perfect clips begins the separate requalification trajectory rather than modifying the completed extended trial.
The requirement to derive the clips from one YouTube video is primarily a clip-source selection rule.
The complete lesson or story criteria are independently testable content standards rather than attributes of the batch assignment.
The clean, simple editing criteria belong to the independent visual-editing Requirement.
The white-text and exact-font corrections belong to the caption-presentation Requirement.
The removal of animations, flashy transitions, and distracting effects belongs to the clean visual-editing Requirement.
The requirement for each clip to contain a complete lesson or story belongs to the complete-teaching-moment Requirement.
The failure of the remaining clips to use sufficiently impactful moments may also support the independent hook-quality Requirement.
The instruction to match the reference lettering changes the caption-presentation standard rather than the batch assignment.
The requirement that a clip contain a full lesson belongs to the independently testable teaching-moment standard.
The instruction to mix the lesson with B-roll belongs to the B-roll integration Requirement.
Approval for three clips to go live and the associated publication instructions concern approved-clip publishing, not verification of the complete five-clip batch.
Removing the black shadow is a correction to caption presentation.
Removing wind noise is an independently testable audio-cleanup correction.
The 45-to-60-second target changes the clip-duration standard.
The instruction not to cut lessons off halfway belongs to the complete-teaching-moment Requirement.
The post-correction failure concerns text position and should be routed to caption presentation.
The freelancer's upload action implements publication of an approved clip rather than production of the batch.
The completed upload claim belongs to approved-clip publishing.
The warning that earlier-quality videos would not receive approval under the stricter standard concerns the recurring approval gate, not the completed first-live assignment.
The rule that rejected clips are returned, corrected, and excluded until approval primarily defines the approval gate rather than changing the monthly quota.

The new ability to reuse a body clip two to three times with different hooks is an independent variation-reuse behavior; only the explicit return to full-speed work supports RESUME for the monthly quota.
The newly authorized B-roll source and its placement rules are more specifically governed by the Natural B-Roll Integration Requirement.
The source-discovery statement is presented as hook training rather than a change to the allowable YouTube source material.
The praise that moment capturing was spot-on verifies selected moments, not the clips' opening hooks.
The request to find better and more impactful moments concerns source-moment selection rather than hook quality.

The rule allowing a clip body to be reused by swapping its hook or opening belongs to the independently defined clip-variation Requirement; the strong-hook training clause does not materially change the existing hook-quality criterion.

The concrete observed correction concerns a video ending before completing the full lesson; the B-roll clause restates the existing integration expectation without establishing a distinct B-roll failure or change.
Updating Notion with the date and published Reel link is post-publication activity logging, not delivery of the clip review package.
This link reports the published Instagram post rather than submission of a Google Drive review package.
The uncertainty concerns which main-account handle should be used in post metadata, not configuration of the dedicated account.
This is an implementation commitment to upload an approved clip, not evidence about configuring the dedicated account.
This completion claim concerns publishing a clip rather than configuring the dedicated account.
This verifies the visual captions within an edited clip, not the Instagram post caption or account tag.
The requested lettering style concerns text rendered inside the video rather than Instagram post metadata.
The reported moving-text issue concerns the position of captions within the video.
In the supplied local context, this submission follows the requested correction to the position of text within the clips.
The upload-completion claim supports publication of an approved clip but does not establish compliance with the required cadence or peak-hour window.
The instruction to publish clips on the assigned page and send the resulting link concerns Reel publication and reporting to the client, not recording the post on the Notion card.
The statement that the clip was uploaded is an implementation claim for publication, but it does not state that the required Notion activity record was created.

missing_requirement_candidates.description: The client independently states that each clip's views, performance, and engagement are tracked for transparency, but no current Requirement represents that tracking behavior.
